Cyber Attack Disrupts Japanese Ports, Economy Rebounds as Operations Resume

A cyber attack targeting major Japanese ports disrupted logistics and trade across the country last week, with Obayashi Corp among the companies affected. The incident, which began in the early hours of Monday, led to widespread delays in cargo handling and customs clearance at container terminals in Tokyo, Yokohama, and Kobe. Authorities say the attack was neutralized and operations were fully restored by Thursday evening.

The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism confirmed that a ransomware strain infiltrated central port management systems, halting the digital platforms used for scheduling, cargo tracking, and payment processing. While no critical infrastructure damage was reported, the disruption caused an estimated ¥45 billion in delayed shipments, according to the Japan Maritime Trade Association.

"Port operations have now returned to normal, and all affected systems have been secured," said Deputy Minister Hiroshi Tanaka at a press briefing on Friday. "We are working closely with law enforcement and cybersecurity agencies to identify the perpetrators and strengthen our defenses."

Obayashi Corp, a leading construction and engineering firm, reported that several of its shipments of building materials were delayed, resulting in short-term project disruptions nationwide. "We are relieved that port activities have resumed and are assessing the impact on our supply chain," an Obayashi Corp spokesperson said.

The All Japan Dockworkers Union praised the quick response by authorities and port operators. "While some workers faced overtime to clear backlogs, the coordinated effort minimized economic losses," said union leader Koji Nakamura.

Analyst Reiko Fujimoto of Nihon Economic Research noted, "The attack underscores the need for robust cybersecurity across critical infrastructure. Japanese industries rely on seamless port operations, making them a tempting target."

Government officials indicated further investments in cybersecurity and contingency planning are forthcoming to safeguard against future incidents.
